subject: RBAC v2 pilots: customer selection + success criteria (Private + Dedicated)
related_account: IronBank Financial; Northbridge Healthcare; Aegis Insurance Group
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:08 AM PST
Subject: RBAC v2 pilots: customer selection + success criteria (Private + Dedicated)

Hi Aisha / Marcus / David,

We need to lock pilot accounts for RBAC v2 (one Private, one Dedicated) so we can finalize the enablement plan with Sales/SE and keep the rollout timeline credible.

Proposed candidates (from current enterprise pipeline):

Private (VPC/on-prem-ish posture):
- Northbridge Healthcare (Private POC scoping underway; strongest “separation of duties” + audit export requirements)

Dedicated:
- Aegis Insurance Group (Dedicated evaluation; asked explicitly for least-privilege templates + SSO/SAML mapping)
- IronBank Financial (strong fit but their security review appears to be trailing by a few weeks; may not line up with our initial flag window)

What I need from each of you by EOD Wed:
1) Which 2 accounts do we pick (1 Private + 1 Dedicated) and why?
2) Minimum success criteria for a pilot (so we don’t declare victory on “it didn’t break”)
3) Comms plan constraints (what we can/can’t promise, who must be present on customer calls, what evidence we can share)

Draft success criteria (very rough):
- Customer can create/assign role templates without support intervention
- At least one “sensitive workflow” validated end-to-end (e.g., audit export, routing policy edit, key rotation) with expected allows/denies
- “Why denied?” experience is usable (denial reason codes; admin debug header limited to admins)
- Audit log entries include authz decision context (action/scope/decision/policy version)
- No P0 regressions / denial spikes; rollback plan validated

If helpful, I can turn this into a 1-pager for exec + Sales enablement once we align.

Thanks,
Naomi
Product, Security & Compliance PM
Redwood Inference


---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 pilots: customer selection + success criteria (Private + Dedicated)

Naomi,

+1 on Northbridge for the Private pilot. Healthcare buyers tend to be very specific on “who can do what,” and they’ll push on auditability / evidence in a way that will surface gaps.

For Dedicated, I lean Aegis over IronBank for the first flag window if IronBank’s review is slipping. We want a pilot that will actually toggle the feature and exercise it, not one that stays in legal/security limbo.

Security success criteria I’d add:
- Validate break-glass procedure + monitoring in at least one environment (even if it’s internal-only, we should be able to describe it and show logs/alerts)
- Audit export: verify authz decision fields survive through exporter (action/scope/decision/denial code/policy version)
- Ensure we do NOT over-share internals: denial reasons exposed to end users must be constrained; admin-only debug header behind permission
- Explicitly document non-goals to the customer (no custom ABAC rules / scripting; scoping model is org/project/env + predefined roles)

Comms constraint: we should be very careful about stating “deny-by-default everywhere” until we have endpoint coverage gating in CI across the relevant surfaces.

Marcus
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 1:04 PM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 pilots: customer selection + success criteria (Private + Dedicated)

Adding the identity/SSO angle.

Northbridge is good if they’re willing to run the “IdP group -> role binding” setup early. Private deployments tend to have:
- stricter constraints on group naming / attribute availability
- more sensitivity to first-admin bootstrap and safe recovery

If we pick Northbridge, I suggest we explicitly require in pilot kickoff:
- IdP type confirmed (Okta/Azure AD/other)
- exact group claim / attribute they can send (e.g., groups vs roles vs custom attribute)
- test users: at least 3 personas (Security Admin, Operator, Auditor)

On Dedicated: Aegis has been pretty straightforward in my prior interactions (fewer custom requirements). IronBank often asks for very formal change-management + evidence packets, which is fine but can slow the first toggle.

Success criteria (identity-specific):
- Role binding via IdP group mapping works consistently (no “it depends on which service”) across Console + API
- Deprovisioning: remove user from IdP group => permission removed within agreed propagation time (we should define expectations)

David Kim
IT / Identity
Redwood Inference


---

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 8:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 pilots: customer selection + success criteria (Private + Dedicated)

Agree with the direction: Northbridge (Private) + Aegis (Dedicated) as first pilots.

Two exec-level concerns to address in the plan:
1) Safety: If we see denial spikes or an authz regression (including any bypass), we need a clear rollback and customer communication path.
2) Evidence: We should be able to provide credible artifacts for enterprise security reviews coming out of the pilot (design overview, audit log example, and test coverage summary).

Naomi—please draft a short pilot brief (1 page is fine) that includes:
- success criteria (measurable)
- timeline and gating (feature flags)
- who participates on customer calls (Security Eng should join at least kickoff + closeout)
- what we will share vs not share (esp. around internals)

If you can send by Friday, I can use it for next week’s leadership sync.

Aisha
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Executive Sponsor, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 10:32 AM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 pilots: customer selection + success criteria (Private + Dedicated)

Thanks all — I’ll proceed with:
- Private pilot: Northbridge Healthcare
- Dedicated pilot: Aegis Insurance Group
- Hold IronBank as “next up” once their security review timing is clearer

Next steps / comms plan (internal + customer-facing):

Internal enablement (Sales/SE/support):
- I’ll post a pilot brief + FAQ snippet and run a 20-min enablement with the SEs assigned to these accounts (what’s in scope, what’s not, how to troubleshoot denies, when to escalate).
- Marcus: I’d like you on the kickoff call for both pilots and on a short “closeout” call to validate security claims.
- David: please provide a short checklist for IdP group mapping + deprovision expectations (we can include this as a pre-req for Northbridge).

Pilot success criteria (v0.3):
1) Role mgmt + assignments
- Customer can assign built-in templates to at least 3 personas (Security Admin, Operator, Auditor)
- At least one custom role created by the customer (limited scope) without Redwood intervention

2) Sensitive workflows validated (with expected allows/denies)
- Dedicated: edit routing policy OR modify model pinning/rollout policy
- Private: export audit logs to SIEM OR modify retention/residency settings

3) “Why denied?” is actionable
- Denials return consistent code + message
- Admin-only debug header works only for authorized admins; no sensitive leakage to normal users

4) Auditability
- Audit log contains action + scope + decision + denial_reason_code (if deny) + policy version
- Example events exported successfully (we can provide sanitized samples for their security review)

5) Safety
- Feature-flagged enablement with rollback runbook ready
- We track deny rate, authz latency impact, and support tickets during the pilot

Attachments:
- RBACv2_Pilot_Success_Criteria_v0.3.pdf
- RBACv2_Pilot_Comms_Plan_v0.2.docx

Aisha — I’ll follow up separately with the 1-page brief for leadership by tomorrow afternoon.

Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 4:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 pilots: customer selection + success criteria (Private + Dedicated)

All good.

Two minor edits I’d suggest before we socialize broadly:
- In the comms plan, explicitly state the scope model (org/project/environment) and that we’re not offering customer-defined policy scripting in v2.
- Add a line item that we will provide a sanitized audit log sample (allow + deny) showing the authz decision fields, but we will not provide internal policy evaluation traces beyond what’s in the audit logs / admin UI.

I’m available for both kickoffs next week. Just send times when you have them.

Marcus
